text:
Leah: heads-up: hit a rare but reproducible issue where tombstones disappear from slabs during eviction/compaction handoff and cause deleted keys to reappear for a short window. sketch + ideas below.
Marco: oh no. reappearing deletes is bad. TL;DR repro?
Leah: sequence: (1) delete K on node A -> creates tombstone entry in slab (tsn=100). (2) A schedules compaction/evict and frees slab bucket (compact happened asynchronously). (3) tombstone hasn't replicated to B yet. (4) ownership moves to B; B never saw tsn=100 so now reads return older value for K until replication arrives.
Diego: so eviction/compaction physically removed the tombstone before it propagated. this is an interaction between GC (to save space) and replication/handoff.
Asha: similar to stale-value issues but with deletions. Could cause user-visible resurrected keys. What's our current invariants for tombstone retention?
Leah: we keep tombstones until snapshot_retention_ms or until we safely replicate them. but eviction/compaction was freeing memory aggressively because tombstone was in a cold slab region and compactor didn't check replication status.
Marco: options: (1) delay physical freeing of slab memory for entries with unreplicated tombstones until replication acked; (2) propagate tombstone metadata with takeover token so new owners know about recent deletions; (3) maintain ephemeral tombstone cache on node edges to catch reads during handoff. tradeoffs: memory vs complexity vs latency.
Diego: (1) sounds safe but could bloat memory if lots of deletes; we already retain tombstones for retention window but compaction can still evict slabs containing them to disk/evict->free. Need to differentiate logical removal vs physical free.
Asha: (2) is appealing: reuse the takeover-token idea but embed tombstone_highwater=highest_tombstone_lsn for prefix. new owner waits or uses tombstone_highwater to filter reads until it receives missing tombstones. cheaper per-takeover than pinning memory.
Leah: yeah: token carries min_lsn as before but also tombstone_highwater (thw). Readers on old node will stop serving entries with lsn <= thw unless tombstone present. new owner ensures it has tombstones up to thw. pseudocode:
```
// on takeover token
takeover.min_lsn = X
takeover.tombstone_highwater = THW
// read path
if (slab.lsn(key) < takeover.min_lsn) fallback_read()
if (slab.is_tombstone(key) || slab.lsn(key) > takeover.tombstone_highwater) return slab.read(key)
// else we might be missing tombstone: fallback_read()
```
Marco: subtle: slab.is_tombstone may be false if tombstone was compacted out; so we need tombstone_highwater to indicate that any key with lsn <= THW should be considered "possibly deleted" unless new owner proves otherwise.
Diego: how to ensure THW stays bounded? tombstone_highwater could be min of latest stable_lsn and max tombstone_lsn observed. We should avoid exploding it.
Asha: also consider a small ephemeral tombstone shadow: for recent tombstones we keep a tiny bloomfilter per-prefix listing keys deleted in last T ms. Very compact and fast to check; false positives ok (they just cause fallback). reduces reliance on per-entry metadata.
Leah: tombstone-bloom + takeover-thw hybrid seems promising: bloom covers recent deletions that compactor might have freed; takeover.thw ensures new owner knows there may be deletions up to a point. If bloom says maybe-deleted -> fallback_read. False positives are harmless and rare.
Marco: how costly is maintaining bloom per-prefix? we already maintain some telemetry per-prefix; bloom of ~1024 bits per hot prefix is tiny. For cold prefixes we skip.
Diego: fallback_read should prefer route-to-new-owner rather than full disk read. that keeps latency bounded. Also record metric 'reads.blocked_by_tombstone_bloom' and 'takeover.tombstone_wait_ms'.
Asha: ops policy: default retention window for tombstone bloom = 500ms-5s configurable. we keep per-prefix bloom only when deletes per-second > threshold. fallback: route to authoritative for a short grace window (200ms) while new owner syncs tombstones.
Leah: testing: chaos scenario with aggressive compaction and delayed replication; synthetic workload: create key, delete key, force compaction, then takeover quickly. assert no resurrected keys unless forced takeover logged.
Marco: add feature flag runtime.flags.tombstone_shadow_bloom and runtime.flags.takeover_tombstone_highwater. ops-bot: create canary ticket?
ops-bot: created #CANARY-1001: "tombstone-shadow-bloom + takeover-thw canary" assigned to @leah, due 2026-04-18 :white_check_mark:
Diego: corner cases: bloom false negatives (we should size bloom conservatively) may cause missed tombstones; but bloom false negative is unlikely if we use good params. More importantly, if new owner never gets tombstones and we force takeover after timeout, we should emit an event 'takeover.forced_potential-resurrect' for postmortem.
Asha: agree. we also need to update docs: deletion semantics state that deletes are guaranteed visible after takeover unless a forced takeover happened (we record and notify).
Leah: implement plan: 1) thin tombstone bloom per hot prefix (configurable), 2) include tombstone_highwater in takeover token, 3) reader-checks combine slab.lsn vs min_lsn and bloom vs thw, 4) fallback routing to authoritative node, 5) metrics and canary. I'll spike and measure false-positive fallback rate. ETA end of next week with numbers.
Marco: great. also add a small unit test that simulates compaction removing tombstones and shows bloom catching the case.
Diego: +1. keep the fast path common-case cheap.
Leah: thanks all. I'll post a short RFC summary after spike.
Asha: :thumbsup:
